question: Who is the cabinet minister of the Union Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, as of September 2024?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Narayan Rane**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Narayan Rane** is the Union Cabinet Minister of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) as of September 2024.
 
• He assumed office on **July 7, 2021**, after the cabinet reshuffle under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government.
 
• The Ministry of MSME is responsible for the **formulation and implementation of policies** to promote and support small businesses in India.
 
• Narayan Rane is a senior politician and a member of the **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)**, having served in various capacities at both the state and central levels.
 
• Under his leadership, the Ministry has been focusing on **boosting MSME growth through initiatives like technology adoption, financial support, and market linkage programs**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **MSME Sector in India:**

 
 
• The MSME sector is often referred to as the **backbone of the Indian economy**, contributing around **30% of India’s GDP** and employing over 11 crore people.
 
• It includes **manufacturing, services, and trade-based enterprises**.
 
 
 
• **Key Initiatives by the Ministry of MSME:**
 
 
• **Udyam Registration:** A simplified registration process for MSMEs to avail of government benefits.
 
• **Credit Guarantee Fund Scheme:** Provides collateral-free loans to small businesses.
 
• **Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP):** Aims to generate employment through entrepreneurship.
 
 
 
• **MSME Classification:**
 
 
• MSMEs are classified based on investment in plant and machinery or equipment and annual turnover:
 
• **Micro Enterprise:** Investment up to ₹1 crore and turnover up to ₹5 crore.
 
• **Small Enterprise:** Investment up to ₹10 crore and turnover up to ₹50 crore.
 
• **Medium Enterprise:** Investment up to ₹50 crore and turnover up to ₹250 crore.
 
 
 
• **Challenges Faced by MSMEs:**
 
 
• Lack of access to **formal credit**.
 
• Inadequate **technological adoption**.
 
• Skilled labor shortages and competition from **global markets**.
